bull.last: RIVN: argues long. Rivian is deeply oversold with an RSI of 25.4 and trading well below its 20‑day, 50‑day and 200‑day moving averages, suggesting a mean‑reversion bounce. The stock has a high short‑sale volume (53.8% of daily flow) and a moderate short‑interest float (14.5%), creating upside upside potential if a short squeeze materializes. Historically Rivian has delivered strong EPS surprises (28.5% to 9.4% beats) and analysts remain bullish, with a mean price target of $19 and 20 buy ratings versus 5 sells. Upcoming earnings on 2026‑10‑29, positive initial R1T reviews, and the new NXP microcontroller partnership add fresh catalysts that could trigger a sharp move up, which the options market already prices at an 11.68% upside.

bear.last: RIVN: Rivian (RIVN) sits at $11.605, well below its 20‑day ($13.10), 50‑day ($14.69) and 200‑day ($15.53) moving averages, confirming a strong downtrend. The stock’s RSI of 25.4 signals oversold conditions but also reflects weak buying pressure and a lack of conviction from the market. Despite a 53.8% short‑sale volume on the latest day, overall short interest is only 14.5% of float with a modest 6.4‑day cover ratio, suggesting the short squeeze narrative is not fully supported. Fundamental metrics are alarming: net margin –54.95%, operating margin –50.4%, gross margin 7.5%, and a free‑cash‑flow deficit of $1.924 B, all under a debt‑to‑equity of 0.89, indicating severe cash‑burn and balance‑sheet strain. Upcoming earnings on 2026‑10‑29 could easily miss expectations given the company’s historically negative earnings and the risk that the VW partnership may be marginalised by Volkswagen’s software shift, which would further erode revenue outlook.

pm.last: RIVN: PASS. RIVN is reporting earnings tomorrow (2026-10-29 amc) and is in a strong long-term downtrend while trading below all major moving averages. Although it is deeply oversold (RSI 25.4), our desk has a poor track record on earnings plays and mean reversion in this market, and the risk of a severe gap down outweighs the expected value.
